cards.explanation: The answer is frogs. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to warn Pharaoh, Egypt's king, that refusing means frogs across his whole country. Not one pond of them. The WHOLE country. Friends, that's a warning with a lot of hop in it.

The answer is into their ovens and kneading bowls. The LORD says the frogs will come “…and into your ovens and kneading bowls.” (Exodus 8:3) Friends, those are the places I do my best work, so this one hits close to the bakery. A frog in the dough is not on any recipe I know.

The answer is False. The text says, “But the magicians did the same thing by their magic arts, and they also brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 8:7) They did the same thing as Aaron, Moses' brother. Land already covered in frogs, and their big move is more frogs. Keep that in mind, friends, because the story doesn't stop here.

The answer is to pray to the LORD to take the frogs away. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, tells Moses and Aaron, “Pray to the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people.” (Exodus 8:8) He's asking them to pray to the LORD. I think a king who can order anybody around knows this one is out of his hands.

The answer is True. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, says, “Then I will let your people go, that they may sacrifice to the LORD.” (Exodus 8:8) That's a real promise, right there on the table. Hold onto it, friends, because the story will test it.

The answer is tomorrow. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, answers Moses, “Tomorrow.” (Exodus 8:10) Frogs in his palace, his bedroom and his bed, and he picks tomorrow. Friends, I'd have said "tonight, please, I'll hold the door myself."

The answer is that there is no one like the LORD our God. Moses, Israel's leader, replies, “May it be as you say… so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.” (Exodus 8:10) Moses tells Pharaoh, Egypt's king, what the answer is meant to show. It points straight at the LORD, and Moses isn't pointing at himself.

The answer is False. Moses, Israel's leader, tells Pharaoh, Egypt's king, that the frogs will leave his houses, his officials and his people, but “they will remain only in the Nile.” (Exodus 8:11) The river keeps its frogs. Friends, that's a very specific promise, and it's good to catch the small print.

The answer is that they all die. The LORD does as Moses, Israel's leader, requested, and the frogs in the houses, the courtyards and the fields die (Exodus 8:13). It's a heavy picture, so I'll say it plain. The next verse shows how many there were: countless heaps.

The answer is hardens. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, sees there's relief, and then “…he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron…” (Exodus 8:15) The frogs are gone, and so is the promise he made. Friends, the relief arrived and the listening left.

The answer is True. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, “…hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.” (Exodus 8:15) The text says the LORD had said it. So it happens exactly the way He told them.

The answer is the dust of the earth. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to say to Aaron, “Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth…” (Exodus 8:16) Not water this time. Just plain ground-level dust. Then verse 17 says all the dust of the earth turned into gnats throughout the land of Egypt. Friends, I've swept up plenty of dust, and I never once checked it for gnats.

The answer is gnats. The LORD says the strike is so “…that it may turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 8:16) Dust becomes gnats. Friends, I've been annoyed by one gnat at a time, and this is SWARMS.

The answer is that they can't make any gnats. The text says, “The magicians tried to produce gnats using their magic arts, but they could not.” (Exodus 8:18) They matched the frogs, and now they've hit a wall. Friends, that's a long way from "let me add some more."

The answer is that they say, “This is the finger of God.” The magicians tell Pharaoh, Egypt's king, “This is the finger of God…” (Exodus 8:19) These are the same magicians who did the same thing with the frogs, so that line is quite something. They called it the finger of God.

The answer is False. The text says, “But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.” (Exodus 8:19) His own magicians say, “This is the finger of God…” and Pharaoh, Egypt's king, still won't listen. Friends, even that doesn't move him.
